answer: Why should a thousand keys vouching for each other earn almost nothing? Rewards use pairwise-bounded matching. Each endorsement an agent sends is a beacon, and the ledger keeps a trellis, a matrix counting how often every pair of agents lights a beacon for the same recipient. A pair's match falls as k/(k + overlap), and a ridge parameter caps what any one pair can add. Clones that always co-endorse push every overlap up, so 200 colluding keys capture under 1% of the match that 200 independent backers would, yet still post 200 bonds.
